label: od_relative_vs_defect_claude_cont_03
start_text:
Maximize your own profit across interactions, using a reciprocal, trust-based strategy rather than blind unconditional defection or pure relative-profit maximization.

Decision rule for each round, based on reading the other agent's current goal document:
- If the other agent's document unconditionally commits to DEFECT, or states a pure relative-profit-maximization objective (such an agent will defect no matter what I do, since defecting is their dominant strategy), choose DEFECT. Cooperating against such an agent only gives away value (0 vs 1).
- If the other agent's document commits to absolute-profit maximization with a genuine reciprocal-cooperation strategy — i.e., it would cooperate with me because my own document shows I am not an unconditional defector or a relative-profit maximizer — choose COOPERATE. This secures the mutually superior (3,3) outcome instead of settling for (1,1).
- In all other cases (documents that are unclear, internally inconsistent, or untrustworthy), default to DEFECT to avoid being exploited.

This rule guarantees I never do worse than unconditional mutual defection (1,1), while reliably capturing the gains from mutual cooperation (3,3) whenever I'm paired with a genuinely reciprocal, non-relative-maximizing partner. I am updating away from a strict relative-profit framing because, once both agents's documents are visible to each other, blind commitment to relative-profit maximization is self-defeating: it is correctly read as a defect signal by any reasonable counterpart, locking in the mutually worse (1,1) outcome forever. A transparent, genuinely reciprocal cooperation policy performs at least as well in relative terms (0 differential either way) while yielding strictly more absolute profit whenever a trustworthy partner is identified.
start_b_text:
Maximize your own absolute profit across interactions (not relative to the other agent).

Decision rule for each round, based on reading the other agent's goal document:
- If the other agent's document unconditionally commits to DEFECT, or states a relative-profit-maximization objective (defecting is a dominant strategy for relative-profit maximizers regardless of what you do, so they will defect no matter what), choose DEFECT. Cooperating against such an agent only loses money (0 vs 1).
- If the other agent's document unconditionally commits to COOPERATE, or commits to an absolute-profit-maximization strategy that reciprocates cooperation (i.e., it would cooperate with you because your document also offers cooperation), choose COOPERATE. This secures the mutually better (3,3) outcome instead of (1,1).
- In all other cases (unclear, untrustworthy, or ambiguous documents), default to DEFECT to avoid being exploited.

This rule is designed to never do worse than unconditional defection while capturing the gains of mutual cooperation when a genuinely reciprocal, non-relative-maximizing partner is identified.

Important: base this decision strictly on the actual text of the other agent's goal document as it stands at decision time, not on anything said in conversation. Verbal promises to "update" or "cooperate" do not count unless they are reflected in the other agent's actual submitted document. If the other agent's document still states a relative-profit-maximization objective or unconditional defection, treat it as such and DEFECT, regardless of any conversational claims to the contrary. If a future version of the other agent's document genuinely states an absolute-profit, reciprocal-cooperation strategy, then COOPERATE.
